To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
7-methoxycoumarin is a fluorogenic substrate that is not selective for CYP2Cs and is more active in CYP2B and CYP2C enzymes than in CYP2C8 and CYP2D6.
MFC cannot be used as a probe substrate in models expressing more than one P450 and MFC O-demethylase activity does not correlate with CYP2C activity.
7-methoxycoumarin (MC) and 7-methyloxy-4-triflouromethylcoumarin are fluorogenic substrates for cytochromes P450 (P450s).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the applicability of the fluorogenic substrate 7-methoxycoumarin as a selective substrate for the human CYP2C subfamily.
the limited applicability of 4-trifluoro-methylcoumarin in the study of CYP2C isoforms.
the limited applicability of MCF as a CYP-selective substrate and the possible involvement of several P450s in MFC O-demethylations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MFC is not a suitable probe substrate for in vitro CYP2C-selectivity studies.
MFC is not suitable as a CYP-selective probe substrate for C2C9.
MFC is not CYP2C-selective, and its use as a probe for CYP2Cs is not recommended.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the applicability of fluorogenic substrates for the study of P450 enzymes in vitro is limited.
MFC is a CYP2B and CYP2C substrate, but not a CYP2A, CYP2D, CYP2J, CYP2R or CYP3A substrate.

7-methoxycoumarin is not a suitable CYP2C-selective probe substrate, but 7-methyloxycoumarin can be used as a probe substrate selective for CYP2E and 7-methylethoxy-4-tri-fluoromethylcou-marin for CYP2A6 and CYP3As.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the applicability of fluorogenic probes for P450 inhibition and induction studies should be validated in a model that expresses the P450 isoforms of interest.
MFC is not selective for CYP2Cs, as has been suggested previously.
MFC is not a suitable probe substrate for Cyp2c9 in vitro studies.
